newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BCE grain prices begin downward correction.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BCE grain prices begin downward correction.

text.p: Most grains futures prices of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) began a downward correction on Wednesday which dealers said was justified after four consecutive days of rises this year.
"The rally of the last few days was more than surprising for many and it ended with a very sharp (downward) turn," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
Maize prices dropped by the 400-forint limit for all maturities and Herczeg added there was still a considerable downside in current prices.
"They could go down by as much as 3,500 to 4,000 forints," he said.
The main reason remains the one million tonne maize surplus at a time when there is very little demand.
"The only buying interest is for some 50,000 tonnes from the Czech Republic," Herczeg said.
Milling wheat prices also dropped by the daily maximum as limited export outlooks could not give further support.
Market players recently said there was some buying interest from Bosnia and Serbia but this was not significant, Herczeg said.
"We are only talking about some truckloads here," he said. "Dreyfus has a 35,000 tonnes shipload of wheat in (the Romanian port of) Constanta it is trying to sell in Novi Sad, with no luck so far".
Wednesday's total turnover was a modest 293.46 million forints or 660 contracts, of which some 400 contracts were for milling wheat.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
